predictions.claim: SBX is bound by CPU. Resident ∞ is bound by memory.
predictions.metric: record.json `binding` and the failed §8 condition at each arm's first failed default-point rung (SBX: host CPU busy ≥ 90% or pace/latency failing with MemAvailable well above the floor; resident ∞: memory_floor, a host-memory/memory-budget refusal or an OOM kill)
predictions.falsifiedBy: SBX's first failed rung bound by memory (memory_floor, host-memory refusal or OOM), or resident ∞'s first failed rung failing on pace/latency with binding=cpu while MemAvailable stays above floor + 1 GiB
predictions.note: Metal: SBX 3.599 core-s/call, resident ∞ 3.548 core-s/call at N=8; both CPU walls at about N = 384–448 (burst model). Resident ∞'s memory bound is 2042–3309 sessions (usable 3.776e+05 MiB ÷ footprint 184.9 max / 114.1 median MiB), far above its CPU wall. CALIBRATION CONCERN, recorded before measurement: calibration expects resident ∞ to be CPU-bound on metal too, so the resident half is expected to be falsified at the default point.

predictions.claim: SBX holds more sessions than resident ∞ at the default point. Predicted ranges: SBX N_max in [384, 448]; resident ∞ N_max in [384, 448].
predictions.metric: ladder.json n_max (SPEC §8, class-matched condition 4, primary rule) per arm, default point
predictions.falsifiedBy: n_max(SBX) ≤ n_max(resident ∞); separately, either arm's n_max outside its range falsifies the numeric part
predictions.note: SBX: burst model [384, 448] (RECOMMENDED; eff 0.4–0.5 of 96 vCPU, refitted on the preliminary default, long, short and no-infra outcomes -- no single eff explains all 11, the best match 9 of 11); pessimistic factor bound [186.7, 236.3] → ladder [160, 192]; average-CPU bound [1223, 1376] (information). Resident ∞: burst model [384, 448] (RECOMMENDED; eff 0.4–0.5 of 96 vCPU, refitted on the preliminary default, long, short and no-infra outcomes -- no single eff explains all 11, the best match 9 of 11); pessimistic factor bound [179, 226.5] → ladder [160, 192]; average-CPU bound [1241, 1396] (information); memory bound [2042, 3309]. CALIBRATION CONCERN, recorded before measurement: the ranges coincide -- the arms differ by 0.05164 core-s/call (1.5%), within the model's resolution, so calibration expects a tie within one ladder step; the direction is SPEC §11's and is kept.

predictions.claim: Resident 300 s comes within one ladder step of SBX, in either direction. Predicted range: resident 300 s N_max in [384, 448].

predictions.note: CPU: the resident per-call CPU and the burst model's resident range [384, 448]; cold wakes (2.3/session-h) cost about one lifecycle each (0.03107 core-s, metal bench), under 0.1% of the per-session CPU. Memory: 3.776e+05 ÷ (114.1 × 0.5611) = 5897 sessions, not binding.

predictions.claim: METHOD, NOT A PREDICTION: the two verdicts reported per arm and point, fixed before measurement.
predictions.note: The preliminary method, unchanged, plus the metal procedure (SPEC §13: ladder to 1024, warm-up 1200 s for SBX and resident arms (control 600 s), footprint drift on summed VM memory, SH_MAX_RUNS 2048). Metal per-arm values (B; primary limit; absolute limit; N=1 overhead): sbx B 115.1 ms, limit 345.2, abs 365.1, overhead 33.69 ms; resident-inf B 126.2 ms, limit 378.5, abs 376.2, overhead -27.84 ms; resident-300 B 123.8 ms, limit 371.4, abs 373.8, overhead -26 ms. ABSOLUTE-TEST EXPECTATION: sbx: N=1 overhead 33.69 ms vs abs limit B + 250 = 365.1 ms, N=8 p95 excess 131.8 ms; resident-inf: N=1 overhead -27.84 ms vs abs limit B + 250 = 376.2 ms, N=8 p95 excess 93.98 ms; resident-300: N=1 overhead -26 ms vs abs limit B + 250 = 373.8 ms -- unlike the preliminary run (SBX N=1 overhead +186 ms against an abs limit of 479 ms; SBX n_max_abs 1), SBX's overhead on metal is small beside B + 250, so n_max_abs is expected to track n_max for every arm.

predictions.claim: The m7i.metal-24xl run shows the largest SBX gain: n_max(SBX) / n_max(resident ∞) at the default point on metal is larger than on the preliminary nested instance, where it was 1 (8 / 8, primary).
predictions.metric: n_max(SBX) / n_max(resident ∞), default point, primary verdict; metal vs preliminary
predictions.falsifiedBy: a metal ratio ≤ 1 (the preliminary primary ratio)
predictions.note: Preliminary default n_max: SBX 8, resident ∞ 8, resident 300 s 8 (primary); absolute SBX 1, resident ∞ 8 (ratio 0.125). Draft metal ratio from 2: [0.8571, 1.167]. Lifecycle on metal: no-op bench 0.03107 core-s/Exec (preliminary 0.0991, 3.2×); SBX − resident ∞ per-call CPU at N=8 0.05164 core-s (preliminary 0.218). CALIBRATION CONCERN, recorded before measurement: the lifecycle term is now ~1.4% of SBX's per-call CPU, so both arms meet the same CPU wall and calibration expects a ratio of about 1 -- the primary claim (ratio > 1.0) is expected to be falsified or tie; on the absolute verdict the metal ratio is expected to rise from 0.125 to about 1.

predictions.claim: At mem512, resident ∞ is bound by memory and SBX holds more sessions than resident ∞. Predicted ranges: resident ∞ N_max in [320, 320]; SBX N_max in [1, 1].
predictions.metric: ladder.json n_max (primary) per arm at the mem512 point; record.json binding of each arm's first failed mem512 rung (with e15.slice memory.events high/oom for resident ∞)
predictions.falsifiedBy: resident ∞'s first failed mem512 rung not bound by memory (neither memory_floor, a memory-watchdog abort, nor e15.slice MemoryHigh throttling with Exec timeouts), or n_max(SBX) ≤ n_max(resident ∞) at mem512
predictions.note: Resident ∞: footprint at N=8 median 1024 MiB (max 1024), usable 3.774e+05 MiB → N = [368.6, 368.7] → ladder [320, 320], bound by memory (its CPU wall is ~384). SBX: 4.06 core-s/call at N=8 → CPU (burst model scaled by 3.599/4.06) ladder [320, 384]; page cache: 3.776e+05 MiB ÷ 512 MiB = 737.5 sessions (per-inode, no sharing); EBS once uncached: 512 MiB × 64.0% × 0.01744 calls/s = 5.718 MiB/s per session, 1017 MB/s ÷ that = 169.7 sessions. Capacity bound N_sbx = min(CPU, max(cache, disk)) → ladder [320, 384] (CPU (burst)), information only. SBX mem512 N=8 calibration rung: holds False (p95 excess 1895 ms vs primary 752.9 / abs 501 ms; 0 failures; host CPU <1%; disk mean 5.592 MB/s). CALIBRATION CONCERN, recorded before measurement: each new SBX session's FIRST scan reads its own fresh 512 MiB data.bin from EBS (~2.5 s added; later scans hit the host page cache, ~0.5 s), the class medians absorb only the warm cost, and ~6% of window calls are such cold scans at any N (session starts and window calls both scale with N), so calibration expects SBX to fail mem512 at every N > 1: the predicted SBX range is [1, 1], and prediction 9's 'SBX holds more' half is expected to be falsified (resident ∞ holds N=8, p95 excess 95.97 ms).
